The problem: Show that every integer z is generated by 5 and 7.

"Generated by 5 and 7" means every integer can be written as a linear
combination 5a + 7b for integers a, b. This is Bezout's identity since
gcd(5,7)=1.

Let me just answer directly.

Problem. Show that every integer $z$ is generated by 5 and 7 (i.e., every
integer $z$ can be written as $z = 5a + 7b$ for some integers $a, b$).

Proof.

Since $\gcd(5, 7) = 1$ and $1 = 3\cdot 7 - 4\cdot 5 = 7\cdot 3 + 5\cdot(-4)$, we
have the Bézout relation

$$1 = 5\cdot(-4) + 7\cdot 3.$$

Multiplying both sides by an arbitrary integer $z$ gives

$$z = 5\cdot(-4z) + 7\cdot(3z).$$

Setting $a = -4z$ and $b = 3z$ (both integers whenever $z$ is an integer), we
obtain

$$z = 5a + 7b.$$

Since $z$ was an arbitrary integer, every integer is generated by 5 and 7. $
\blacksquare$

PROOF COMPLETE
